about: Questions to the player, numbered once and never reused. The lead is the only writer. Wording is in play terms: what the original does, what ours does, what to do. answered rows keep their answer and outcome.

questions.title: Archers marking themselves as firing
questions.outcome: Merged 85611ebf: archers mark themselves firing as the original does.

questions.title: Soldiers changing places: whole rule vs the auto-resolved yardstick
questions.answer: auto-resolve weighs troop types; a fought battle has counters (crossbows one-shot knights, waste on peasants), so its verdict is no yardstick for a fought one
questions.outcome: Merged: the whole changing-places rule, oracle-checked; the fought check no longer demands the auto-resolve's winner.

questions.title: Do the computer's archers shoot while marching?
questions.answer: nothing to answer; waits on Q4
questions.outcome: Merged. On the field and lane your save was dealt, ours ends the no-orders battle exactly as the original did: 60 of 129 defenders left, attacker destroyed.

questions.title: One battle with no orders, saved at start and end
questions.outcome: Filed as noorders-start and noorders-end fixtures.

questions.title: Two End Turns in a game with Advanced Farming on
questions.inplay: Advanced Farming is the new-game option that changes how your fields work each season. Every save we have was played with it off, so those farming rules have never been checked against the original.
questions.todo: Start any new game with Advanced Farming on and play through two End Turns. Nothing else is needed. The game's own autosaves from that point are the two saves one turn apart the End Turn check needs; I will copy them from the install.
questions.ask: Reply: Q5 after the second End Turn
questions.outcome: Merged: your saves are the fifth End Turn pair. Every Advanced Farming rule the turn runs agrees; the one difference is the weather roll, which no save carries.

questions.title: Saving a game never finishes
questions.answer: type a name, click Save: the wait text appears, the dialog stays until thumbs-down, and Load lists no such game
questions.outcome: Merged: a refused save now repaints, as the original does. Saving mid-battle is its own row; Q9 asks which screen you were on.

questions.title: Relaunch the stopped siege-army work
questions.outcome: Merged: the siege residual was a defaulted save import, not an AI or battle rule; the End Turn check went from 271 to 278 of 279 fields.

questions.title: Relaunch the stopped screen-position audit
questions.outcome: Merged: every draw we could pair by coordinate sits exactly where the original draws it (115 of 115); the check is stored and tested. The near misses were the instrument's, not the screens'.

questions.title: When the save failed, was a battle on screen?
questions.inplay: In the original you can save from the battlefield menu bar in the middle of a battle. Ours refused that save silently, which looked like a hang. Both halves are now fixed and merged: a refused save repaints, and a mid-battle save writes and loads back onto the battlefield with the same battle running.
questions.todo: Only to confirm the diagnosis: were you on the battlefield or the campaign map when you typed the name and clicked Save? If the map, the cause is still unknown and I will reopen it.
questions.ask: Reply: Q9 battle, or Q9 map
questions.outcome: So the mid-battle refusal was not your case. The cause is still unknown; Q10 asks for one more try on a current build, which now shows what it refuses.

questions.title: Save once more from the campaign map on a current build
questions.inplay: Your save from the map wrote no file, and nothing we tried reproduced it. Two things changed since: a refused save now paints its reason instead of sitting on the wait text, and saving is no longer refused on the battlefield.
questions.todo: Build from current main, play to the campaign map, File then Save, type a name, click Save. Note exactly what the box shows next: the name in the Load list, or a message, and its words.
questions.ask: Reply: Q10 saved, or Q10 with the message shown
questions.outcome: The refusal did not recur. The three-second wait is filed and in flight; the original saves near instantly.

reports.text: The player starts on the east side of Quantville; in the original always west.
reports.outcome: Merged: each new game now re-rolls as the original does; west three games in four.

reports.text: Saving a game never finishes and no file appears.
reports.outcome: Fixed and merged twice over: a refused save repaints, and saving mid-battle now works as in the original (C237). Q9 asks which screen you were on, to confirm the cause.

reports.text: Saving takes about three seconds; should be near instant.
Tutorials come back on every launch.
reports.outcome: In flight: how the original remembers it (L2.INI) comes first.

reports.text: The AI raises three armies and they just sit; in the original the knight takes a county in the first year.
reports.outcome: Filed with your autosaves; next free seat.
